name: Knocker
description: A small, wrinkled, miner-clad subterranean fairy of Cornish and Devon folklore, said to inhabit mines and to make knocking sounds in the rock — sometimes guiding miners toward rich tin or copper veins, sometimes warning of imminent collapse, and sometimes maliciously punishing whistlers or thieves.

aliases.name: Bucca
aliases.meaning: related Cornish folk spirit sometimes equated with the knocker

aliases.name: Tommyknocker
aliases.meaning: American adaptation of the Cornish knocker by Cornish miners in Colorado, Nevada, California, and Pennsylvania

aliases.name: Berggeist / Bergmännlein
aliases.meaning: 'mountain spirit / little mountain man' — German mining-spirit counterpart

aliases.name: Kobold (mining sense)
aliases.meaning: specifically the underground/mine kobold, parallel to the knocker

origin: Concentrated in Cornwall and Devon (England) and Wales, with diaspora presence in mining communities of Pennsylvania, Colorado, Nevada, California, Wisconsin, and Michigan, USA — wherever Cornish 'Cousin Jack' miners settled.
